label: Planarian
plain: A freshwater flatworm that regrows its whole body from a fragment. Its protein atlas is of Schmidtea mediterranea; the outlines drawn are of a planarian in general, with indicative sizes.

modelled.text: Cells models a generic cell and a sheet of such cells, not this animal. The sheet stands for skin-like tissue and is drawn on the worm for the scales only. The brain and the worm are placeholder outlines: nothing at those scales is simulated.

levels.note: The cell drawn is one cell of the sheet, which stands for skin-like tissue; it is not a model of a planarian's skin cell. Its shape and its sizes are the picture's choice: six flat sides where it meets its neighbours, an outer face and a base, about 20 µm across and as tall as the sheet's cells. The plate under the layer marks where a flatworm's skin rests on a basement membrane, which Cells does not model.

notes.text: One cell of the skin-like layer
Its flat-sided shape is the picture's choice

levels.note: The sheet stands for skin-like tissue: a single layer of cells. It is drawn lying over the brain of the placeholder worm for the scales only; the simulated sheet is not that animal's tissue.

notes.text: The sheet stands for skin-like tissue: a single layer of cells

levels.note: The outline drawn is a planarian flatworm's brain with its two nerve cords, as a placeholder. The sheet of cells stands for skin-like tissue lying over the brain, drawn on the worm's head so that the scales follow one another; it is not the worm's tissue. The brain's own cells are neurons and glia, which Cells does not model. The size of the brain is the picture's choice: no measurement of it was read.

sheet_mark.note: The sheet, to scale: it stands for skin-like tissue over the brain

notes.text: A planarian's brain and nerve cords: a placeholder outline
The brain's own cells, neurons and glia, are not modelled

levels.note: The outline drawn is a planarian flatworm, about 10 mm long, as a placeholder. The sheet of cells stands for skin-like tissue and is drawn on the worm's head for the scales only. Its length is the picture's choice, within the 1 to 14 mm of the animals that one study of Schmidtea mediterranea used; its width and its proportions are the picture's choice, and no measurement of them was read.

notes.text: A planarian flatworm: a placeholder outline

lu2025.text: Lu J, Xu H, Wang D, Chen Y, Inoue T, Gao L, Lei K (2025) 3D reconstruction of neuronal allometry and neuromuscular projections in asexual planarians using expansion tiling light sheet microscopy. eLife 13:RP101103. The intact animals it used, of the clonal asexual strain CIW4 of Schmidtea mediterranea, were 1 to 14 mm long.
